reviews.title: Disappointed and No Longer Shopping Here
reviews.content: I used to love Target—not just for the convenience, but because it felt like a company that genuinely cared about inclusion and equity. That’s why I was so disappointed to learn they’ve rolled back their DEI (Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion) commitments.Target once made strong public promises to support marginalized communities, hire more equitably, and partner with diverse suppliers. Now they’ve quietly ended those goals, shut down their REACH program, and stepped away from external accountability. It feels like they’re turning their back on everything they claimed to stand for.I don’t support companies that only show up for communities when it’s profitable. This rollback sends a clear message: they’re more concerned with pleasing critics than doing what’s right.I won’t be shopping at Target anymore. I expect better from a company that once prided itself on being a leader in inclusion.

reviews.title: Target Location
reviews.content: Target Location - 13700 San Pedro Ave, San Antonio, TXWe ordered a water filter replacement for our fridge online. The new filter was defective, and when we put the old filter back in, it worked. So we are sure it was the filter that is defective. We tried to print the UPS return label from the target platform, and it was ALSO defective. We could not actually get a return label, it kept taking us to UPS websites and log ins and just not working. So I was forced to go into the store. THEN, at the store, they have the audacity to tell me the Apple card I brought was not the card used on file (which it 100% was, they ended up refunding the money to the card). I had a back and forth with the manager and the employee kept enforcing that I was wrong, stating that they have to go with what their system says. Well, when you system is wrong and broken, no wonder people arent shopping with you anymore. After pulling up the order details, the manager was able to refund the money back on the card, but not without a TON of headache. And it was the right card, thats the part that gets me. All limbs of target seem to be broken, and I will never shop at Tarjay again, sadly. I get its not the employees fault.

reviews.title: I have loved Target for years but this…
reviews.content: I have loved Target for years but this last experience takes the cake.  I ordered something on sale, got confirmation, went to pick it up at the store.  They couldn't find it and had me waiting for almost an hour while they looked, I finally had to leave.  Talked to customer service and after about 20 minutes she agreed with me that the item WAS on sale, after telling me many times that it was not.  She was willing "as a one time courtesy" to let me order it again and "match" the price--though the price she gave me was $4 more than the sale price.  For no reason.  So I've wasted a lot of time on this through absolutely no fault of my own.  This has totally disillusioned me on how much I used to like Target.  I hate Walmart but I'm going back, I've never been hassled like this there.

reviews.title: Ordered a small 8 ft round pool on May…
reviews.content: Ordered a small 8 ft round pool on May 3. Didn't get it set up until after Memorial Day as we had a cold spring.  When filling with water noticed the ground soaking wet.  discovered the center seam was not fused together in one spot This was not noticeable when setting up.  Took pool down and dried it out for a few days and packaged it up and took it to my local Target.  They could not do the return because it was one day past the return window even though it was defective.  Apparently the 90 day return policy does not apply to things ordered online which is only 30 days as I found out. They were not willing to accommodate me in any way.  I'm stuck with it!  Target used to be a customer friendly and accommodating retailer.  That is no longer the case.  They ought to be ashamed of themselves.

reviews.title: I recently had my credit card number…
reviews.content: I recently had my credit card number stolen. The thief bought a $250.00 gift card on Target.com. When I called Target to try to stop the charge I was told by customer service that people can purchase a Target gift card on line anonymously. They don’t have to provide a name address or email so they can’t be tracked. Because I didn’t have the order number they couldn’t help me stop the charge. Almost every company I have dealt with stops this type of purchase by blocking with a fraud alert so someone can’t just purchase a gift card especially on line anonymously! They also don’t have a security person to talk with about any concerns of this nature. I just wanted to put this problem out there for others to be aware of . Buyer beware this company will not help you if you have a stolen credit card!

reviews.title: NEVER GO TO THE SOUTHFIELD MI TARGET…
reviews.content: NEVER GO TO THE SOUTHFIELD TARGET LOCATION!!! I spoke with manager who didn't want to hear it and basically blamed me and said "there's nothing he can do." I WILL NEVER SHOP HERE AGAIN

reviews.title: Bought a sealed iPad, received a Samsung tablet, and got humiliated at the store
reviews.content: I had one of the worst customer experiences of my life at the Target store in Eatontown, NJ.My sister bought what was supposed to be a brand new iPad, paid in cash, and received a sealed Apple box. When we opened it at home, there was a Samsung tablet inside — not even close to the product we paid for.We returned to the store with the receipt, the box, and the incorrect tablet, and instead of helping us, the staff laughed, accused us of fraud, and refused to take any responsibility. We were calm and respectful, but treated as if we were trying to scam them.We’ve filed formal complaints with BBB and New Jersey Consumer Affairs, and we won’t stop until this is resolved.It’s not just about the tablet — it’s about the complete lack of respect and accountability from a company as large as Target.

reviews.content: I ordered towels, received the wrong colors and towels that appeared to have been washed and returned. The towels were mislabeled, with UPC numbers and color names that did not match and were not the colors I ordered. When I reordered, I again received mislabeled and wrong .color towels, although these hadn't been washed/returned. When I complained and asked for compensation or correct colors (I bought the towels for a charitable auction), I was told it wasn't their problem and so suck it up. As if their capitulation to Trump's nonDEI policy wasn't enough to let everyone know where Target stands, this abdication of responsibility for labeling and the delivery of wrong products -  which I paid several hundred dollars to have shipped to Ecuador - certainly paints a clear picture of Target's refusal to accept responsibility for its policies and mistakes.

I am requesting that the originally advertised price of $350 be honored or that a more reasonable adjustment be made to reflect fair and honest business practices. I will no longer shop at a store that price gouging up to $145 which is crazy.

One of the item was missing the CD so I took it back to the store for exchange or return. The male manager said that according to the store policy this item cannot be returned and they don’t have another one in store for exchange. I have to go to another Target store TRY to exchange it and there is nothing he can do. He also mentioned that people tampering with the item right in front of my nieces. He acts like this is my problem and the store policy doesn’t hold any responsibility or any value of the merchandise sold in store. I never in my life even bother to waste my time on this kind of issue, especially only $15, but it’s a great lesson not to go to this store ever.This is first time I trying to write a review. reviews.title: Can target listen to their customer?
reviews.content: I am hoping Target will read the review, since they don't provide email address for customer to provide their feedback.Target card customer service is a pain to deal with. I am hoping they will train their employee better- to help them understand how US system works.I called in to their credit card service since I have not yet received my new card, and had hard time getting into the online system to figure things out.The people who picked up calls (I called 4 times) were all having Indian accent. While I have nothing against where the customer service locates, I experienced the lack of understanding of the situation since they are not US based.   Here is my experience:  they asked me to verify my SSN and then my address. Apparently I gave her my SSN. And she just could not pass me on the address part. I lived in a single family house, with address something like 808-A.  But somehow in Target/USPS system has it registered as 808 "Apt" A. So when I told them my full address but said the number as 808-A rather than "808 apt A", this rude lady told me to call back until I figure out my own address.  That was literally her words. "Call back until you remember your address."I told her I am 100% sure the address is correct. In addition, SSN should be a more important and a much more sensitive info than the address, so why would she block me out because of the address.  I then asked to speak to someone else (manager/transfer to some US based customer service). She said since I don't have correct address, there is no way anyone can help me out, and she HANG UP the phone while I was still talking."Luckily" I recalled to said my address as "apartment" so I finally was able to "pass" their check after I called again. But that was after hours of communication.Really? when someone already passed the SSN, and said the full address including the street name, town, state and zipcode, except saying the address number in a different way, that counted as "incorrect"? and you hang up on your customer?Fortunately, I live in a place that we have so many other options so Target is not our main to-go anymore.  after this, I am totally moving away from Target. and will advise my friends to avoid dealing with Target as well.

reviews.title: Target 360 membership and same day delivery is a SCAM
reviews.content: The Target 360 membership offers unlimited same day deliveries. The membership is $10.99/month or $99/year if paid annually. Without the membership, same day delivery costs $10 for any order, and with the membership it's free for orders $35 and above (the $10 cost applies for any orders under $35 even with the membership).I utilized this service for the first time the other day, spending over $35 with same day delivery. So I was surprised when later I was being prompted by Target to "review and tip [my] shipt shopper." I ignored the prompt initially, but was then forced to review AND tip before I could access target.com. Turns out that Target has fully outsourced the same day delivery service to a third party, where Shipt "shoppers" go into the stores and pick out the orders and deliver them, and therefore require a tip. It's ridiculous.First off, it's not clear from the outset when signing up to the 360 membership that that's how it works. Secondly, I don't want a personal shopper (I'm picking out the items myself anyway); why are Target employees not pulling the orders from the shelves for same day deliveries? And finally, all of the above points aside, if paying $10 for same day delivery OR paying for a 360 membership to get free same delivery on orders over $35, the cost of the service should be covered. To expect people to tip on top of this is highway robbery. (I was not able to move past the prompt to review and tip the shipt shopper.)Do better, Target.

reviews.content: The order and pickup service was unreliable. After arriving at the store, I realized the in-store price was much higher than the online price. I still don’t understand why they acted that way—it was one of the worst customer service experiences I’ve had."

reviews.title: Target plus item responsibity
reviews.content: My son purchased an HP laptop for $1,295.99 through Target, and the item was delivered to the store on March 20th. He picked it up on March 23rd. Unfortunately, he needed to return the item but missed the return window because he had to go to the ER and was later hospitalized. When we realized the laptop still needed to be returned, we went to the Target store on April 19th, but they said the return window had closed on April 18th.I checked Target’s website, which states that most items have a 90-day return window. However, since this was a Target Plus item, the store directed me to call Target Guest Services at 1-800-591-3869. When I called, they told me I needed to contact HP directly. I then called HP customer service, but they said they couldn’t help because the item was purchased through Target.I contacted Target again, and this time they gave me another number for a Target specialist (1-612-307-8330), but that number didn’t work. I called Guest Services again at 1-800-591-3869, but they still couldn't help me.In summary: I strongly advise against buying Target Plus items. The return process is extremely frustrating, with both Target and third-party sellers refusing to take responsibility. Also, the way Target advertises a 90-day return policy for “most items” is misleading and confusing for customers.

reviews.title: This card is not worth it
reviews.content: This card is not worth it. Please, seriously consider a different option. Not only is the APR outrageous, but the customer support is less than 1 star. Let me give an example.The website to pay the Target Store credit card went down for maintenance. During the time the website went down, no payments could be made. They did say that all late fees due to the website being down would be waived. The time period that the website was down was the time period that I pay my bill every month. I have had this card for a while and never missed a payment or had a late payment. When the website was back up and running, I made a payment and it went through just fine. That was less then two weeks after my initial try.When I went back to the website the next month to pay my bill, I noticed there was a late fee. I called and the customer service I got was dreadful. They blamed me for not paying the bill, even though the website was down. When I mentioned that, they told me it was my fault for basically "Not figuring it out" and told me the late fee would stay. In the middle of the conversation with the Target customer rep, they just hung up on me. That was absolutely wild. I didn't swear or yell. I just wanted to get to the bottom of it.AT the end of the day, it is just a late fee of $30, which is super annoying, but it won't break the bank for most people. But this is just poor practice on Targets part. It is stealing money from families because Target decided to do work on a website and make it unavailable for payments. Target is not out to take care of its customers, but to squeeze them for every penny they can.

reviews.title: Target really sucks
reviews.content: As someone who has held a RedCard for over 10 years, I’ve made countless purchases at Target — from everyday essentials to home decor. Target has long been one of the retailers I relied on the most. However, after my experience with Target’s online customer service today, I’ve completely lost confidence in this company.The customer service I encountered was not only unprofessional but also surprisingly rude. The way I was treated made it clear that customer satisfaction is no longer a priority for Target. I’ve also been a customer of Walmart and Amazon, and by comparison, Target’s service is a complete disappointment.What frustrates me the most is that after so many years of loyalty and spending, I was met with indifference and poor attitude when I needed help. Good customer service should be the foundation of any reputable company — and this experience made me realize how far Target has fallen in that regard.Because of this, I will be significantly reducing my spending at Target. reviews.title: Thought I could trust shopping at…
reviews.content: Thought I could trust shopping at Target but no one should. Went in to buy a Visa gift card and as I was driving home opened the package to discover a completely different card inside with the activation code glued to the fraudulent card to complete the fraud. I immediately called the number on the back of the package for InComm to report the fraud and stop the activity on the card and returned to the Target store. At the store I showed the manager what I had and as I showed him the section where I pulled the card from, we saw two more identical packages. He opened those and they too were tampered with and had fake cards inside. After sending both companies ( Target and InComm ) pictures of what I had, they each tell me that they can’t do anything about it and refer me to the other. In the end neither company is standing up for the fraud and I’m out $100. Buyer beware! Target no longer is the reliable store I remember.

reviews.title: Accusation of stealing at Target
reviews.content: On April 1st, 2025, I visited the Target location near Court Square in Long Island City, New York, where I had an unpleasant experience involving an accusation of theft. As I was completing my checkout, a store employee approached me and asked, "Are you going to pay for the hair ties?" reviews.title: Target cancelled a delivery based on Lies
reviews.content: Target cancelled a delivery based on proven lies. Then, Customer Service would not allow me to talk, and spoke to me in a demeaning, accusatory manner.I ordered 10 items from Target, which has delivered to me for the past 6 years. The delivery never came, and no one contacted me. They claim they came to my door. I live in a concierge building, and when a delivery comes, the concierge calls me. They did NOT come. They claim they tried to reach me and I was "unavailable". I found out (the hard way), that Target subcontracts its deliveries  to Shipt. Evidently, although Target agreed Target has my correct phone number, apparently Shipt did not.They charged my card. When I called CS, they insisted Shipt tried to reach me and deliver the order, even after I explained how  my concierge, and Target, both had my correct number. I never knew about Shipt, nor how they got my number wrong. The CS person said Target would not contact Shipt with my correct number. They said I must navigate that, myself. I replied that I had nothing to do with Shipt, and if Target hires them to make the Target deliveries, they must give their subcontractor, Shipt, the correct delivery info. The CS agent would not cooperate, and insisted I must track down Shipt. According to the Customer Service agent, Ella, everything was my fault, no apologies, no empathy. Just insistence  that I was wrong, that I was lying, and I should contact Shipt.  So I will not use Target any more. This complaint is a warning for others.

Corporations are people, aren't they? So say something, not just profit off the representation of these groups.
